ge from 100 m to 200 m. headward escarpments are well imaged in both map and cross-section views. proximal facies of the mass transport deposits includes rotated blocks and large angular glide blocks. these pass distally into smaller glide blocks and chaotic seismic facies inferred to be debrites. intermediate parts of the mass transport deposits have longitudinal linear features parallel to inferred flow direction. distal patterns consist of transverse compressive ridges. other mass transport deposits too large to be completely imaged within the 3d survey show internal facies, consisting of large angular glide blocks in a matrix of seismically visible smaller blocks and chaotic facies inferred to be debrites. multiple causes of mdts in this area are probable. in possible order of importance, these include tilting and oversteepening of sediments because of tectonic uplift, high sedimentation rates at the mouth of the canyon, and eustatic falls of sea level. key words: upper quaternary, seafloor, mass-transport deposits, mass transport deposits, base of slope, offshore niger delta, deepwater nigeria, leveed- channel deposits, sediment waves, seismic facies, debrites, digital enhancement, volume rendering, pressure ridges, lateral flow lines, shear zones, fault scarp, rotated blocks, thrust blocks mass-transport deposits in deepwater settings sepm special publication no. 96, copyright © 2011 sepm (society for sedimentary geology), isbn 978-1-56576-287-9, p.
